adds.title: Gambia Criminal Code Section 147(1) - Brusubi Magistrates' Court ruling, March 2026
adds.summary: Gambia Criminal Code Section 147(1) (Cap 10:01, 2009) makes gross indecency between males, defined in Section 147(3) to include any homosexual act whether in public or private, a felony punishable by a mandatory five years' imprisonment, and in March 2026 the Brusubi Magistrates' Court applied that provision to convict two men for same-sex conduct on 18 May 2025 in Old Yundum and imposed five-year prison terms with no reduction under Section 34 of the Criminal Offences Act, expressly holding that claimed rights to gender identification and LGBT rights do not legalize homosexuality in Gambia and that such acts in public or private remain punishable to protect societal norms and morality.

adds.title: Human Rights Watch
adds.summary: In 2017 Gambia's government promised not to prosecute consensual same-sex acts, contrasting with prior anti-LGBT rhetoric, but retained laws criminalizing same-sex conduct including the October 2014 law imposing up to life imprisonment for "aggravated homosexuality" offenses.
